verdicts.title: DpProcess.__or__ walks the whole process tree on every composition, making heterogeneous accountant accumulation quadratic
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on the current tree with the prebuilt extension (.venv). Every link verified: _base.py:405-415 _has_same_repeated_pld materialises Repeated(self,count)._pld_cache_key(); _base.py:379 default _leaf_and_count returns (self,1) and neither Composed nor CachedProcess overrides it (only Repeated does, _repeated.py:51); Composed._pld_cache_key -> iter_cache_key (_composed.py:43-46) is a full stack walk that descends into CachedProcess.inner (_iter_cache_key.py:30-34); __or__ :499-503 calls it on the accumulated spine on EVERY composition. git show 4bfd0c16 confirms the exact swap from `if left_leaf == right_leaf` to `_has_same_repeated_pld`. Measured `Accountant() | poisson(gaussian(1.0+0.001*i), 0.01)`: n=125 0.064s, 250 0.241s, 500 0.929s, 1000 4.07s - clean 4x per doubling. Control with `DpProcess._has_same_repeated_pld = lambda self, other, count: self is other or self == other`: 200 0.0033s, 400 0.0063s, 800 0.0095s, 1600 0.0193s, 3200 0.0392s - linear. Homogeneous path unaffected: 20000 identical compositions in 0.075s. Verified the DPTrainer is on the homogeneous path (_dp_trainer.py:287 `ctx.accounting |= ctx.step_process` with a single reused step object; the periodic `acc.cached(...)` wraps leave the spine bounded). Severity stays low: no wrong result, no epsilon change, and the documented loop in Accountant's docstring and docs/reference/accounting.md is homogeneous, so only a per-step-varying schedule pays. Not a duplicate of #911 (that issue is Monte Carlo calibration cost, a different code path).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A research script or per-step noise schedule folds heterogeneous steps into an Accountant: `for i in range(N): acct = acct | dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(sigma_i), q)`. No two steps merge, so the Composed spine grows and each `|` re-walks it via Repeated(spine, 2)._pld_cache_key(). Measured on this tree: 250 steps 0.24s, 500 steps 0.93s, 1000 steps 4.07s (quadratic), versus 0.003-0.04s for 200-3200 steps with the pre-#883 equality test (linear). Extrapolating the fitted quadratic, 10,000 heterogeneous steps costs several minutes and 50,000 costs hours of pure bookkeeping, with no warning and no indication the cost is in `|`. Results are numerically unchanged; the DPTrainer and any loop reusing one step object are unaffected.

verdicts.title: calibrate()'s runtime-safety fallback re-runs the whole adaptive search without the union bound, while still reporting the undivided mc_failure_probability
verdicts.reasoning: Verified in source and reproduced on a REAL Monte Carlo mechanism, not just a stub. Source: calibration.py:301-309 builds probe_config with mc_failure_probability/(max_iterations+2) and runs the first bisection under it; :321-323 opens `with _use_discretization(overall_config)`; :331-339 re-runs the FULL `_calibrate_impl` inside that context when the runtime re-evaluation is unsafe, and takes `achieved = result.achieved` from that second adaptive search; :350-351 stamps `result.mc_failure_probability = overall_config.mc_failure_probability` whenever the final PLD is MC-backed, regardless of which branch ran. So the union bound the code deliberately applies to the first search is dropped for the second, while mc_confidence still claims to cover it. Real-mechanism repro (b_min_sep BandMF, bands=4, n_steps=40, epsilon_budget(3.0, delta=1e-3), mc_resolution=5e-3, mc_failure_probability=1e-2, max_iterations=30, spy on Budget.evaluate): the fallback fired in 6 of 10 seed/p0 combinations, each time with ~25-30 probes at beta/32 followed by ~25-29 probes at the FULL beta=0.01, e.g. Counter({0.0003125: 28, 0.01: 28}), and the returned result reported mc_confidence=0.990000. The honest simultaneous bound for that fallback search is 1 - 28*0.01 = 0.72. Default-config arithmetic in the finding also checks out: resolved_num_mc_samples is 2,940,252 at beta=1e-6 and 3,417,797 at beta=1e-6/102, so probe-vs-runtime differences are estimation noise with no systematic sign, which is why the fallback fires roughly half the time. docs/reference/accounting.md:731-734 states verbatim the property the fallback discards ('result.mc_confidence therefore covers the adaptive search as a whole'). Severity medium, not high: the error is in the reported confidence level attached to epsilon, not in epsilon itself, and it only affects MC-backed processes (b_min_sep, balls_in_bins, MF Gaussian with MC PLDs); but the direction is fail-open and the overstatement is 25-100x. The secondary 'roughly doubles the probe count' observation overlaps open issue #911 (Monte Carlo calibration performance), but the confidence-accounting defect is distinct and not tracked there, so already_tracked is 0.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Calibrating any Monte-Carlo-backed process (e.g. BandMF + b_min_sep) with calibrate(). Roughly half the time the probe-config bisection's result is not privacy-safe when re-evaluated under the runtime discretization, and calibrate() silently re-runs the entire bisection under overall_config, i.e. with EVERY probe at the full mc_failure_probability instead of beta/(max_iterations+2). The returned param and achieved then come from that unprotected adaptive search, yet result.mc_confidence still reports 1 - beta. Observed directly: b_min_sep at beta=1e-2, max_iterations=30 ran 28 probes at 3.125e-4 followed by 28 probes at 1e-2 and returned mc_confidence=0.99, where the simultaneous bound over the 28 deciding probes is at best 0.72. At the library defaults (beta=1e-6, max_iterations=100) a team publishing 'epsilon = 3.0 at delta = 1e-5 with Monte-Carlo confidence 1 - 1e-6' from result.mc_confidence is overstating that confidence by up to ~100x on the fail-open side. Epsilon itself is unchanged; the failure probability attached to it is understated.

verdicts.title: CalibrateResult.achieved can violate the documented isclose(achieved, target, rel_tol=tolerance) contract while reporting converged=True
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced twice: once with a stub budget and once with a real Monte Carlo mechanism. Source verified: calibration.py:324-325 computes `achieved = budget.evaluate(final_process)` under overall_config; :326-330 re-checks only privacy-safety; :340 `result.achieved = achieved` overwrites the converged probe value with no closeness re-check; _calibrate_impl (:474-534) hard-codes converged=True and is the only place the isclose test is applied. Both docstrings (calibration.py:136-142, and the 'relatively close' wording) and docs/reference/accounting.md:722-725 ('math.isclose(achieved, target, rel_tol=tolerance, abs_tol=0.0) is true') still assert the old invariant. Stub repro: CalibrateResult(param=1.000000, achieved=0.500000, target=1.000000, iterations=1, converged), isclose False. Real-mechanism repro (b_min_sep BandMF bands=4, n_steps=40, epsilon_budget(3.0, delta=1e-3), tolerance=1e-6): in the four of ten seed/p0 combinations where the fallback did NOT fire, achieved came back as 2.9768990653998104, 2.999839744431425, 2.9858047534416134 and 2.982586082209384 against target 3.0 - drifts of 5e-5 to 8e-3 relative, all failing isclose at rel_tol=1e-6 while converged=True. Direction is always privacy-safe (achieved <= target is re-checked at :326-330), so no under-noising; the defect is the contract and the reported convergence quality. Severity low: no epsilon or privacy impact, and the existing test test_reported_achieved_is_runtime_upper_bound only asserts achieved <= target and equality with the runtime re-evaluation, so nothing in the suite catches the broken isclose claim.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: For any Monte-Carlo-backed process, calibrate() returns converged=True with an `achieved` that is a fresh runtime-discretization re-measurement rather than the converged probe, so the documented postcondition math.isclose(achieved, target, rel_tol=tolerance, abs_tol=0.0) is false. Measured on b_min_sep BandMF at tolerance=1e-6 and target epsilon 3.0: achieved 2.9769 / 2.9826 / 2.9858 / 2.9998 in the four of ten runs that did not take the recalibration fallback - relative gaps of 5e-5 to 8e-3 against a 1e-6 tolerance. A downstream assertion of the documented contract fails, and a run card claiming 'calibrated to within 1e-6 of the target' is wrong by up to ~0.8%. The direction is privacy-safe (over-noised), so no epsilon guarantee is broken.

verdicts.title: A checkpoint budget silently overrides a stricter template budget on Accountant restore, leaving budget_exceeded on the looser cap
verdicts.reasoning: The mechanics reproduce exactly as claimed: saving Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(10.0, delta=1e-5)) after 5 x eps_delta(0.5, 1e-7) and restoring into Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(1.0, delta=1e-5)) yields restored._budget == EpsilonBudget(10.0, 1e-05), epsilon_at(1e-5) == 2.499990499950025 and budget_exceeded == False. Source confirmed at _accountant.py:238-250 (checkpoint budget unconditionally replaces the template's, with only logger.warning) and :207-224 (budget_exceeded returns False for `self._budget is None` with no tri-state). I could not confirm this is a DEFECT rather than a deliberate design choice, which is why this is PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED: (a) packages/opaque-accounting/tests/test_budget_serialization.py:85-99 explicitly pins checkpoint-wins plus the warning as intended behaviour; (b) the warning does reach stderr in a bare process via logging's lastResort handler - I saw it in the repro - so 'silently' overstates the case; (c) no documented contract is violated: docs/reference/accounting.md:74-93 covers budget checkpoint codecs but says nothing about template-vs-checkpoint precedence; (d) I verified the DPTrainer is unaffected - it constructs bare Accountant() at _dp_trainer.py:280-281 and restores with opaque_from_state_dict(Accountant(), ...) at :5537, so no budget key is ever written or restored there. What remains is a genuine asymmetry (template wins when the checkpoint has no budget, loses when it has one) and the unlanded half of the OPQ-302 fix sketch, i.e. budget_exceeded still cannot distinguish 'no cap configured' from 'my cap was replaced'. That is a defensible API-hardening request, not a demonstrated fail-open bug.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A caller resumes with `from_state_dict(Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(1.0, delta=1e-5)), saved)` where the checkpoint was written by an accountant carrying epsilon_budget(10.0, delta=1e-5). The restored accountant keeps the checkpoint's looser cap: restored._budget == EpsilonBudget(10.0, 1e-05), epsilon_at(1e-5) == 2.4999905, budget_exceeded == False, so a `while not acct.budget_exceeded` loop runs well past the intended epsilon <= 1.0. A WARNING line naming both budgets is emitted (and reaches stderr by default), and an explicit test pins this precedence as intended, so the operator is not left with no signal at all - the exposure is limited to harnesses that suppress or never read WARNING logs, and only when the caller deliberately passes a different budget on restore. The DPTrainer resume path never writes a budget key and is not affected.
